hints: Filter on two things: the restaurant is vegetarian, and its closing time is 23:00 or later.
Sort by rating, highest first. Check where NULL ratings land: Postgres puts NULLs first in a descending sort unless you say otherwise.
`ORDER BY rating DESC NULLS LAST, name`
sampleDataSql:
INSERT INTO restaurants (restaurant_id, name, is_veg, closes_at, rating) VALUES
  (1, 'Green Bowl', TRUE, '23:30', 4.5),
  (2, 'Midnight Grill', FALSE, '23:45', 4.8),
  (3, 'Sattvik Rasoi', TRUE, '22:00', 4.9),
  (4, 'Leaf & Ladle', TRUE, '23:00', 4.1),
  (5, 'Moonlit Thali', TRUE, '23:15', NULL);
schemaSql:
CREATE TABLE restaurants (
  restaurant_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  is_veg BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
  closes_at TIME NOT NULL,
  rating NUMERIC(2,1) -- NULL until the restaurant has reviews
);
statement:
A food delivery app wants a **"late-night veg"** shelf. It should list every vegetarian restaurant that closes at **11 pm or later**. All closing times are before midnight.

Return each restaurant's `name` and `rating`, best-rated first. Restaurants without a rating yet go **last**. Break ties by name, A to Z.
title: Late-Night Veg Kitchens
